name: Tokitsukaze and Meeting
description: Tokitsukaze is arranging a meeting. There are $$$n$$$ rows and $$$m$$$ columns of seats in the meeting hall. There are exactly $$$n \cdot m$$$ students attending the meeting, including several naughty students and several serious students. The students are numerated from $$$1$$$ to $$$n\cdot m$$$. The students will enter the meeting hall in order. When the $$$i$$$-th student enters the meeting hall, he will sit in the $$$1$$$-st column of the $$$1$$$-st row, and the students who are already seated will move back one seat. Specifically, the student sitting in the $$$j$$$-th ($$$1\leq j \leq m-1$$$) column of the $$$i$$$-th row will move to the $$$(j+1)$$$-th column of the $$$i$$$-th row, and the student sitting in $$$m$$$-th column of the $$$i$$$-th row will move to the $$$1$$$-st column of the $$$(i+1)$$$-th row. For example, there is a meeting hall with $$$2$$$ rows and $$$2$$$ columns of seats shown as below: There will be $$$4$$$ students entering the meeting hall in order, represented as a binary string " 1100 ", of which ' 0 ' represents naughty students and ' 1 ' represents serious students. The changes of seats in the meeting hall are as follows: Denote a row or a column good if and only if there is at least one serious student in this row or column. Please predict the number of good rows and columns just after the $$$i$$$-th student enters the meeting hall, for all $$$i$$$.
input_specification: The first contains a single positive integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \leq t \leq 10\,000$$$) — the number of test cases. For each test case, the first line contains two integers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$ ($$$1 \leq n,m \leq 10^6$$$; $$$1 \leq n \cdot m \leq 10^6$$$), denoting there are $$$n$$$ rows and $$$m$$$ columns of seats in the meeting hall. The second line contains a binary string $$$s$$$ of length $$$n \cdot m$$$, consisting only of zeros and ones. If $$$s_i$$$ equal to ' 0 ' represents the $$$i$$$-th student is a naughty student, and $$$s_i$$$ equal to ' 1 ' represents the $$$i$$$-th student is a serious student. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n \cdot m$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$10^6$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, print a single line with $$$n \cdot m$$$ integers — the number of good rows and columns just after the $$$i$$$-th student enters the meeting hall.
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1677B — Tokitsukaze and Meeting [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
